Your team projects 60.8 points, or 69.0 with the armband on Haaland. That captain choice is marginal — he's 0.3 clear of Salah — but the model backs him, and there's a real tail: an 8% chance he scores 2 or fewer, against a 25% chance of 10+. Hold him unless you have fresh information before kickoff.

You're anchored to Arsenal and Liverpool, with three of the former and two of the latter in your XI. That's heavier concentration than most managers will run, but both clubs scored prolifically last season and the model sees no reason to trim. The rest spreads across Manchester City, Bournemouth, Newcastle, Chelsea and Nottingham Forest.

Don't transfer. Nothing clears its own cost. You have a free transfer banked and 0.5m in the bank, but the bench projects only 10.7, with Mykolenko at 3.1 as your only genuine cover. That's fine for Gameweek 1.

Remember: every projection here is built on last season's data. Injuries, managerial changes, departures, and lost places between May and now aren't in these numbers. Watch team news before the deadline.

Your team projects 69.0 with the armband on Haaland. That figure rests entirely on last season's data—scoring rates, start frequency, and club strength—so it does not yet account for summer transfers, managerial changes, or shifts in playing time. Treat all projections as provisional until the first matches are played.

Haaland carries the armband 0.3 points clear of Salah. He has an 8% floor (2 or fewer points) worth noting, but an 8% ceiling above 10 makes him the model's choice. Salah at 7.9 remains close enough that either captain could be right; the gap is narrow.

Your outfield sits 3-4-3. Arsenal and Manchester City each field two outfield players in your eleven, and Liverpool two. The bench's best score is Mykolenko at 3.1, well short of displacing anyone above. No trade improved on holding—your squad as built is your best use of the budget. You have one free transfer and £0.5m in the bank if you find a need.

Your eleven projects 60.8 points, rising to 69.0 with the armband on Haaland. He sits 0.3 clear of Salah and carries a 25% chance of hitting double figures, though an 8% chance of falling to 2 or fewer tempers that upside. No transfer clears its cost, so you are holding your free move.

Three Arsenal players and two each from Liverpool and Manchester City give you meaningful exposure to last season's strongest sides. That clustering is deliberate and backed by the projections, but it does mean your fortunes lean heavily on how those three clubs start. Wood on the bench at 4.2 is your closest reserve; Mykolenko at 3.1 offers little.

Every figure here rests on last season's data alone—starting rates, scoring patterns, and team strength. None of it knows about summer signings, managerial changes, or shifts in form. Palmer and Semenyo are your freshest assets by that lens, but their projections are built on what they did before, which may not hold. The same applies to everyone: treat the rankings as informed, not certain.

You are set up to attack. Haaland and Salah carry the weight, your midfield is deep, and the bench is thin by design. Unless the early teamsheets surprise you materially, there is no case for moving.
